quizKeys.q: Which glycolytic enzyme is not used in gluconeogenesis?
Where is pyruvate carboxylase located?
Which tissue releases newly made glucose into the blood?
Aldolase has ΔG′° = +23.8 kJ/mol, yet it runs in both directions in the cell. Why?
quizKeys.key: Its products are kept at low concentrations, so ΔG in the cell is close to zero

quizKeys.q: What is ΔG′° for pyruvate kinase run in reverse?
Why don’t bypasses 2 and 3 need ATP?
quizKeys.key: They are hydrolyses of phosphate esters, which are already favorable

quizKeys.q: Starting from pyruvate, why does oxaloacetate leave the mitochondrion as malate?
quizKeys.key: There is no oxaloacetate transporter, and malate also carries reducing equivalents for cytosolic NADH

quizKeys.q: Starting from lactate, where is oxaloacetate converted to PEP?
quizKeys.key: In the mitochondrion, by mitochondrial PEPCK

quizKeys.q: Why can’t muscle glycogen raise blood glucose directly?
Which of these can humans convert into net glucose?
Why can’t acetyl-CoA give net glucose in animals?
quizKeys.key: Pyruvate dehydrogenase is irreversible, and the two acetyl carbons are lost as CO₂ in the citric acid cycle

quizKeys.q: Which amino acid is exclusively ketogenic?
How many high-energy phosphates (ATP + GTP) does it take to make one glucose from 2 pyruvate?
Which step of gluconeogenesis consumes NADH?
Why is glycerol a cheaper precursor than lactate?
quizKeys.key: It enters at DHAP, skipping the ATP- and GTP-consuming steps between pyruvate and 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate

quizKeys.q: What does fructose 2,6-bisphosphate do in the liver?
Acetyl-CoA builds up in the liver during fasting. What is the effect?
quizKeys.key: It activates pyruvate carboxylase and inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase

quizKeys.q: What is a substrate (futile) cycle?
quizKeys.key: Two opposing reactions running at the same time, with net hydrolysis of ATP

quizKeys.q: How does glucagon lower fructose 2,6-bisphosphate in the liver?
quizKeys.key: PKA phosphorylates PFK-2/FBPase-2, activating its phosphatase activity

quizKeys.q: After about a day without food, most blood glucose comes from…
Why does glucagon inactivate pyruvate kinase L?
quizKeys.key: So PEP made by gluconeogenesis isn’t converted straight back to pyruvate

quizKeys.q: What is the net cost to the body of one turn of the Cori cycle?
Besides carbon, what does the glucose–alanine cycle carry to the liver?
During a fast, where does the liver get the ATP to run gluconeogenesis?
